title: Crispi Gnocchi in Sweet Pepper and Basil Sauce
description: Potato gnocchi cook directly in a creamy white bean and sweet pepper sauce, finished with fresh basil and Parmesan.
equipment: Ninja Crispi PowerPod with US Bake preset
Ninja Crispi 4-quart glass container with adapter

ingredients.name: shelf-stable potato gnocchi
ingredients.note: Small plain gnocchi labeled for a 2–3 minute simmer; choose a lower-sodium brand.

ingredients.name: peeled roasted red bell pepper
ingredients.note: Fully softened, seedless, and plain without vinegar or brine.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: Use plain mushroom broth made with mushrooms and water.

ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves
ingredients.note: Loosely packed; leave out coarse stems.

ingredients.name: cooked cannellini beans
ingredients.note: No-salt-added beans, rinsed, drained and weighed after draining.

steps.title: Set up the Crispi
steps.text: Use the room-temperature 4-quart Crispi glass container with its large-container adapter. Leave out the crisper plate so the food sits in liquid. Load the container before starting the PowerPod and keep the storage lid off during cooking.

steps.title: Blend the pepper sauce
steps.text: Blend {beans}, {pepper}, {garlic} and {broth} together in a deep jug until smooth and pourable.

steps.title: Nestle in the gnocchi
steps.text: Separate {gnocchi} directly into the unheated glass and pour the pepper sauce over them. Spread evenly and press down so all pieces are coated and sit below the sauce surface.

steps.title: Cook together on Bake
steps.text: Fit the large-container adapter and PowerPod and select Bake. Stir after 10 minutes. Once the sauce visibly bubbles around the gnocchi, cook for the package simmer time, usually 2–3 minutes. Split one to check that the center is tender; continue in 2-minute intervals if needed. Allow 15–27 minutes total.

steps.title: Make the basil cream
steps.text: Ladle a little warm pepper sauce into a deep heatproof jug and blend with {basil}, {parmesan} and {cheese} until smooth.

steps.title: Bind the remaining sauce
steps.text: Ladle the loose pepper sauce into the HexClad, leaving plenty clinging to the cooked gnocchi. Bring it to a simmer, whisk in the stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the gnocchi
steps.text: Take the skillet off heat, fold in the basil cream and gently lift the hot gnocchi into the finished sauce. Divide the saucy gnocchi between bowls.

notes: Make ahead: Blend the pepper sauce a day ahead and refrigerate. Add the basil at the finish to preserve its flavor. For dairy-free gnocchi, omit the Parmesan and cream cheese. Blend the basil into the thickened pepper sauce and choose dairy-free gnocchi. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Gnocchi can become dense after freezing and reheating. The blended pepper base alone freezes well for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the gnocchi to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: If already frozen, thaw overnight in the refrigerator and follow the fridge reheating directions. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 445 kcal, 19.2 g protein, 85.2 g total carbohydrate, 2.7 g fat, 9.8 g fiber, 647 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
preferredMethod: Ninja Crispi PowerPod with US Bake preset

steps.title: Allow for oven timing
steps.text: Use the first time given as a check. A covered metal dish may need 3–10 minutes longer; check tenderness or the center temperature every 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the covered baking dish
steps.text: Preheat Samsung Bake to 350°F. Use a small metal baking dish and a fitted cover or foil to retain moisture.
